ES.label: S&P 500 Fut
ES.source: S&P 500 E-mini September contract, -19.00 points, Perplexity real-time feed stamped 11:07 UTC, priced off Tuesday's 7642.75 settle. Modest on its own; the point is what it is NOT doing. Overnight brought a confirmed-fatality tanker attack in the Strait of Hormuz, a fresh three-decade high in Japanese 10-year yields, a 15-year high in the German Bund, the Nikkei down 2.85% and the Korean market down roughly 3% - and US large-cap futures are down a quarter of one percent. That gap between the severity of the headlines and the shallowness of the futures response is the single most useful observation on this board. NOT ATH: the cash index is 2.148% below its record close of 7798.99 set 8/13/26 and 2.148% below the 7816.70 record intraday high from the same session.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Perplexity real-time feed stamped 11:11 UTC, +2.14% against Tuesday's 16.34 settle. Tuesday itself was the move: the index rose 9.52% from Monday's 14.92 close, which FRED's VIXCLS series independently confirms. But read the level, not the change. Sixteen and a half is a below-average VIX. Overnight we got owner-confirmed fatalities on a Saudi tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, an explicit new US policy of striking Iranian tankers in retaliation, Hormuz transit volumes down to four commodity vessels on Tuesday against a ten-day average near thirteen per Kpler, Iranian strikes on targets in Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait - and the S&P's implied volatility is 16.7. The options market is pricing a rates repricing, not a war. That is either the most important piece of information on this page or the biggest mispricing on it, and I do not think anyone can tell you honestly which. What it does mean concretely is that portfolio insurance is still cheap relative to the tail that is visibly on the table. The Nasdaq's own volatility index closed Tuesday at 21.96, up 8.82%.

US2Y.label: US 2-Year
US2Y.source: MarketWatch, page stamped 'Sep 2, 2026 4:45 a.m. EDT', -0.6 basis points against Tuesday's 4.410 close. Investing.com's 2-year page was rejected today: its prior-close field read 4.35, which is Monday's close, making that page a full day stale. So: 2s10s sits at 40.6bp this morning (4.810 minus 4.404) against 38.6bp at Tuesday's close and 40.4bp Monday. The curve FLATTENED two basis points Tuesday as the front end repriced the September hike, and has re-steepened two basis points overnight as the long end took over. Each leg is quoted from the same vendor on both days - 10-year from Investing.com, 2-year from MarketWatch - so the change is basis-consistent even though the two legs come from different vendors. The percentage on this tile is the change in the yield level, not basis points.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: Perplexity real-time feed, CLUSD, stamped 11:12 UTC - unchanged, one cent lower, against Tuesday's 90.22. And that flat print is one of the two or three most informative numbers in this entire briefing, because of the path it took to get there. Crude rose roughly 5.7% Tuesday on the Hormuz tanker strikes. Overnight it traded as high as 92.28 on the confirmation of two seafarer deaths aboard the Saudi vessel SIDR and on the new US 'tanker for tanker' retaliation doctrine - and then gave all of it back, closing the loop at 90.21. A war premium that spikes and round-trips inside twelve hours is a market telling you it does not expect sustained supply loss, however grim the headlines are. Hold that thought against the Kpler transit collapse, which says the physical disruption is real and current. Those two facts are in genuine tension and I am not going to resolve them for you this morning.

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: December COMEX futures, Perplexity real-time feed stamped 11:10 UTC, -0.94% against Tuesday's 4396.40 settle. Gold fell 2.38% Tuesday and is down again this morning - a third consecutive decline, and spot corroborates at 4308.62, -0.46%. This is the tell of the whole morning and it is worth slowing down for. Tankers are being hit in the Strait of Hormuz with confirmed loss of life, the United States has declared a policy of striking Iranian oil tankers, and Iran has fired on targets in three countries hosting US forces - and gold is FALLING. Gold does not fall on war. Gold falls on real yields. With the US 10-year at a fresh 52-week high, Japanese 10-year yields above 3% for the first time since 1996 and the Bund at a 15-year high, the discount rate is beating the fear trade, decisively. Anyone framing this tape as a geopolitical risk-off event has the mechanism backwards, and gold is the evidence.

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: Perplexity real-time feed stamped 11:14 UTC, -0.35% against Polygon's C:EURJPY Tuesday close of 185.674. The yen is bid, and it is important to be precise about how much: the crosses are down about a third of a percent, against a FIRMER dollar - the dollar index is up 0.35% at 99.78 - and the Nasdaq volatility index closed at 21.96, not in the high twenties. THIS IS NOT A FUNDING SQUEEZE. A genuine carry unwind looks like 1.5%-plus moves in the crosses, a falling dollar and a volatility spike. Today it is a routine bid in a currency whose central bank just told you it will keep raising rates while its 10-year yield printed above 3% for the first time in thirty years. The Nikkei fell 2.85% overnight and that will tempt a carry-unwind narrative today. The tape does not support it.
